newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian rights leaders see little hope for peace.
newsitem.headline: Colombian rights leaders see little hope for peace.

text.p: Human rights activists said on Wednesday that, despite recent statements indicating Colombia may be on the verge of a lasting peace process, they saw little hope for an end to political bloodletting anytime soon.

"We are at a point where there seems to be a possibility of peace," said Carlos Mario Gomez, president of Amnesty International in Colombia. "But what we see is an extended internal confict growing more serious."

Gomez spoke to reporters on the release of Amnesty's annual report, which said more than 1,000 people were killed last year in fighting between the army, leftist guerrillas and right-wing paramilitary groups.

Government officials and left-wing rebel leaders alike have suggested the possibility of jump-starting peace talks following the highly publicized release Sunday of 70 soldiers captured in combat by the country's largest rebel group, the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC).

But Colombia's highest ranking military officer Gen. Harold Bedoya has thrown cold water on the peace process, calling the negotiations for the soldiers' release "a circus," and launching a massive counterinsurgency effort in northwest Colombia.
Police say many of the 27,000 murders in Colombia last year were related to the climate of endemic political violence that has affected the country for more than three decades.
The military and right-wing death squads killed 1,000 "undesireables" last year, while guerrillas kidnapped an estimated 500 people, Amnesty International said.
